To start off, I'm here to stay but it doesn't mean I'll leave my 2nd love. As it is, Voat is still trying to get on its feet which means a little bit less content than expected. This whole affair started with Victoria getting fired which back fired into several communities turning private, Ellen Pao getting sacked--which was supposed to be good news--and the new CEO not changing anything about the decisions the previous management did, which pretty much means all the signatories of the movement getting Ellen sacked was screwed over.

This makes me wonder, why didn't Pao succumb to the interests of the bigger communities and just, in the words of Elsa "let it go?" She's either pretty obstinate, or maybe the upper management just don't care about the interests of the community. But then again, the reasons behind Victoria getting fired was never announced and if anything, the whole affair was done in cloak and dagger fashion. Pao had the option to do something about the decision to fire Victoria or at least clarify the details as to why she was let go but she didn't do either. One would think that going for the latter and letting the community know why Victoria was let go would be a win-win for the management. They get to remove an employee for whatever reason warranting the decision and since the community is privy to the details, the necessity to resort to rendering several major communities inaccessible until investigations are over wouldn't have happened. Heck, we wouldn't be having Exodus 2.0 and the whole drama in the first place! I mean c'mon, the hivemind is reasonable on good days after all.

But perhaps, and here the speculation begins, Pao didn't because she couldn't--at least without risking a lawsuit. If there's any hard rule that protects the community while maintaining boundaries, it is that you're not supposed to share personal information in the site. Sure, you're allowed to thank Obama for any sort of reason, but if the several witch hunts the community is guilty for is any indication, the community is highly discouraged from sharing any information that would lead to the revelation of a user's personal details. The details behind Victoria's sacking was hidden but the fact remains that it is grave enough for management to let her go and seeing the site from a user's point of view, I'd say they're rather lenient with how things usually go, just don't go around breaking the iron rule. No one working for the site is exempted from this.

Sadly, the community took it the wrong way and well, hiding the details behind the sacking of a well-loved and favored emplotee is pretty much salting the wound. Doubly sad was the fact that Pao received most of the flak from a management-level decision that the community just didn't like. I'm pretty sure she was just doing her job and the offense that Victoria did must be pretty big for Pao not to fight the decision to fire her since it would mean a lot of betrayed and thus angry mods. Although actually, I'm damned sure with this one because the new management isn't changing the decisions that Pao did.

So why was Victoria fired? As it is with any issue mired in corporate bureaucracy, the community will ever know. The truth of the matter will be buried underneath layers and layers of papers, proceedings, investigations, and cats such that not even a zombie apocalypse can revive it. In any case, the damage has already been done and the impact of the truth would long have been made irrelevant should it still come to the surface. Justice delayed is justice denied after all.

So what's next? Well it's very much up to us, the otherwise silent lurkers, discontent moderators, and frustrated developers to make use of Voat to our heart's content hoping that history doesn't repeat itself. Populate the front page with shit posts like this one or generate content worth the lulz. It's really up to us to make Voat work.

Mindfulness of breathing:

  1. Focus on the breath.

    A. Pick either a physical sensations (e.g: the rise and fall of the abdomen, the breath passing through the nose, the breath passing the tip of the nose, etc... ), a mental concept ("in" and "out", or a point in space that the breath passes, or the process of the rising and falling of the abdomen, etc... ) or both.

  2. The mind will begin to wander. When you notice it has (a moment of mindfulness) return focus to the breath.

  3. Rinse and repeat.

Sometimes a moment of mindfulness is not enough to let go of thoughts (when trying to return to your anchor) though. In that case, here are a few different techniques that will allow you to bring the mind back to your anchor:

  1. When unskillful thoughts of desire, anger or anxiety arise turn attention toward thoughts of love, compassion or equanimity.

  2. If unskillful thoughts continue to arise then turn attention toward investigating why those thoughts are unskillful. Scrutinize their drawbacks.

  3. If unskillful thoughts continue to arise then simply pay no attention to them.

  4. If unskillful thoughts continue to arise then try and relax the mind and put an end to thought-fabrication through tranquility.

  5. If unskillful thoughts continue to arise then forcefully apply your attention back to your object of meditation. In this final effort, try harder and harder to bring an end to thought-fabrication by forcefully applying your mind back to your meditation object. Then forcefully try and hold your attention on that object for as long as possible.
A simple explanation and guide to Mindfulness meditation.
